settings.title: Flat-Fee Nil T2 Filing for Dormant Consulting Corporations

settings.editor:
Filing for a consulting corporation you stopped using can feel like paperwork for nothing, especially when no invoices went out, the business number is still open, and the obligation did not stop when the engagements did. We file nil T2 returns made for quiet years, for consultants who want the backlog cleared without an engagement letter or an hourly bill, at $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Whether you took a salaried job, went on leave, moved abroad, or simply stopped looking for the next contract, we check the year against invoices raised, expenses claimed and retainers held, prepare the return with its schedules, and have you sign one T183CORP for each year online. Nothing is printed and nothing is posted.

settings.title: What an Unfiled Year Costs a Dormant Consulting Corporation

settings.description_text: Nothing closes an unfiled year except the return. It is still outstanding years later.
The Agency can write and require the return, which turns a quiet obligation into a dated one.
Where no return arrives the Agency can assess on numbers of its own, and only the real return replaces them.
No clearance certificate is issued while a year is missing, so the corporation cannot be dissolved.

settings.editor:
The usual reason a consulting corporation goes unfiled is that nothing happened in it, which feels like nothing is owed. The return is owed anyway, and the gap is what a future accountant, buyer or registrar sees first.

Catching up is ordinary work here rather than an exception. Each quiet year is $300.00 plus HST per tax year, filed oldest first, with one T183CORP signed online for each of them.

settings.title: Which T2 Schedules a Dormant Consulting Corporation Files

settings.editor:
ScheduleWhat it reportsOn a nil yearWhy
Schedule 100Balance sheet informationUsually requiredA consulting corporation that still holds a bank balance, a shareholder loan or issued share capital has a balance sheet to report.
Schedule 125Income statement informationUsually requiredFiled alongside Schedule 100, reporting nil revenue and nil expenses for the year.
Schedule 141Notes checklistUsually requiredRecords who prepared the financial information and on what basis. It accompanies Schedules 100 and 125.
Schedule 50Shareholder informationRequiredMost consulting corporations have one or two shareholders. Each holding 10% or more of any class is listed by name.
Schedule 24First-time filer informationFirst return onlyFiled with the first T2 after incorporation. A consultant catching up several years files it with the earliest one.
Schedule 8Capital cost allowanceOnly with depreciable propertyA laptop or office furniture still on the books is depreciable property. Claiming no capital cost allowance in a nil year is normal.

Source: the schedule requirements the Canada Revenue Agency sets for a T2 return, applied to a consulting corporation with no billings in the year. Last reviewed November 19, 2026.

settings.description_text: Schedules 100, 125 and 141 can be omitted only where there is literally nothing to report. A bank balance alone rules that out.
A single-director, single-shareholder consulting corporation files it with one name on it.
Claiming none in a dormant year keeps the undepreciated balance intact for a year when the corporation earns again.

settings.html:
The year is nil

  • No work was invoiced and no fee was earned in the tax year
  • No subscription, phone, insurance or accounting fee was charged to the corporation
  • No salary, dividend or management fee was paid out
  • No equipment was bought, sold or written down
  • The bank account sat still, or was closed before the year began

The year is not nil

  • An invoice was raised, even one that went unpaid
  • A recurring subscription or phone line kept billing the corporation
  • The corporation paid the owner anything at all
  • A client retainer was taken in or released
  • Interest was credited on a business account

Due either way

  • The T2 return, every year until the corporation is dissolved
  • A T183CORP signed by an authorised signing officer, one per tax year
  • Any open GST/HST account, which files on its own schedule
  • Any open payroll account, which files even at nil
  • The provincial or federal annual return, a separate filing entirely

settings.title: Nil T2 Filing for Consulting Corporations Across Canada

settings.editor:
Dormant consulting corporations are filed the same way wherever the registered office sits, because the return is prepared and transmitted electronically from end to end. There is nothing to print, nothing to post and nothing to sign in person.

Where the corporation was incorporated changes the registry, not the return. An Ontario corporation answers to the Ontario Business Registry, and corporations in British Columbia, Alberta, Quebec and Saskatchewan each answer to their own. The T2 itself is federal and identical in all of them. Within Ontario, a corporation registered in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton or Ottawa is filed on the same terms and at the same price as one anywhere else in the country.

Two provinces add a return the federal T2 does not cover. A Quebec corporation also files the CO-17 and an Alberta corporation also files the AT1. Both are separate provincial returns, and neither is included in the $300.00 plus HST fee.

settings.title: Nil T2 Filing FAQs for Dormant Consulting Corporations

items.item_title: I stopped consulting two years ago. Do I still have to file?
I had no income but I paid for software. Is that year nil?
Should I just dissolve the corporation instead?
I had a payroll account for myself. Does that matter?
Can I file four years at once?
My laptop is still on the books. Does that stop the year being nil?
I invoiced in December and got paid in February. Which year is it?
Does the CRA treat a dormant corporation differently?
What happens if I keep ignoring it?

settings.editor: Yes. The obligation runs until the corporation is dissolved, not until the work stops. Both years are due, each as a separate T2, and each is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.
No. A claimed expense makes the year active, with a loss to report rather than nil amounts. It is worth filing properly, because a non-capital loss carries forward against future consulting income.

That is often the right answer, but dissolution does not skip the filings. Every outstanding year has to be filed before a clearance certificate is issued, and a final T2 is due within six months of dissolution.
It files on its own schedule, separately from the T2, and keeps filing at nil until the account is closed on Form RC145. An open GST/HST account with no returns filed draws its own follow-up.
It matters for payroll, not for the T2. A payroll account stays open until it is closed and expects filings even where no wages were paid. The nil T2 does not close it.
Yes, and most consultants do. They are filed oldest first so balances carry forward correctly, with a separate T183CORP for each year.
No, as long as nothing was bought, sold or written down. Owning an asset is not activity. Claiming capital cost allowance on it would be, so none is claimed in a nil year.
The year it was earned, which for most consulting corporations is the year the work was done and invoiced. That year is not nil, and the one the money landed in may well be.
Only in what the return contains. The deadline, the schedules and the electronic filing requirement are the same as for any other corporation.

The years stay open indefinitely. The Canada Revenue Agency can issue a demand to file and then assess the corporation arbitrarily on figures of its own, which then has to be undone with the real return.
